record.title: Main effects
record.body: Research and marketing center on tendon, muscle, gastrointestinal, and wound repair, with proposed angiogenesis, nitric-oxide, fibroblast, and tissue-healing mechanisms. Most efficacy evidence remains animal or laboratory work; human therapeutic efficacy is not established.

record.title: Side effects
record.body: FDA flags immunogenicity, aggregation, peptide impurities, and API-characterization concerns and finds safety information insufficient for proposed routes. The human adverse-event profile is largely unknown. Angiogenesis or tumor concerns are theoretical, not demonstrated clinical harms.

record.title: Sourcing & pricing
record.body: Public research-quantity listings observed July 25–26, 2026 showed 5 mg at $52 and 10 mg around $92–$97. These prices are benchmarks only. Legitimate research procurement should require lot identity, chain of custody, LC-MS/HPLC evidence, and experiment-appropriate contaminant testing.

record.title: Ongoing research
record.body: NCT07437547 is a recruiting sponsor-submitted Phase 2 hamstring-strain record. NCT02637284 is an older Phase 1 record with unknown status and no posted results. Registration does not validate efficacy, safety, or legality.

record.title: Main effects
record.body: Marketing emphasizes tissue repair, mobility, cell migration, and angiogenesis. RUO TB-500 is a short thymosin beta-4 fragment; research on full-length thymosin beta-4 cannot be transferred to the fragment. Direct human evidence for the fragment is absent.

record.title: Side effects
record.body: FDA reports no human exposure data for the TB-500 fragment and flags immunogenicity, aggregation, and peptide-impurity risks. Its human adverse-event profile is unknown.

record.title: Sourcing & pricing
record.body: Public 5 mg listings observed July 25–26, 2026 ranged from $72 to $78. A product labeled TB-500 should be verified against the actual fragment sequence rather than assumed to be full-length thymosin beta-4.

record.title: Ongoing research
record.body: The NCT07487363 search result explicitly describes itself as a fictional example, so it is excluded as evidence of a real program. Full-length thymosin beta-4 trials are related biology, not direct evidence for TB-500.

record.title: Main effects
record.body: CJC-1295 is a long-acting growth-hormone-releasing-hormone analog. A randomized healthy-adult study demonstrated prolonged growth-hormone and IGF-1 increases, establishing pharmacodynamic activity—not proven recovery, body-composition, or performance benefits.

record.title: Side effects
record.body: FDA notes limited clinical data and serious events including increased heart rate and a systemic vasodilatory reaction. Plausible growth-axis concerns include headache, flushing, edema, altered glucose handling, and cardiovascular effects, but RUO incidence is not established.

record.title: Sourcing & pricing
record.body: CJC-1295 without DAC, 5 mg, was observed at $41 from one public catalog. DAC and no-DAC forms are not interchangeable; identity testing must resolve the actual molecule.

record.title: Ongoing research
record.body: NCT00267527, a Phase 2 program in HIV-associated visceral obesity, was terminated. No active credible interventional program was identified in the registry search.

record.title: Main effects
record.body: Ipamorelin is a ghrelin-receptor growth-hormone secretagogue studied for growth-hormone release and gastrointestinal motility. A randomized Phase 2 postoperative-ileus study provides human context but does not validate broad recovery or performance claims.

record.title: Side effects
record.body: FDA reports serious adverse events, including death, in a literature study using intravenous ipamorelin for gastric motility and says evidence is insufficient for other injectable routes. It also flags immunogenicity, aggregation, impurities, and unnatural-amino-acid concerns.

record.title: Sourcing & pricing
record.body: Public 5 mg listings observed July 25–26, 2026 were approximately $43–$53, including a displayed sale price of $46. List price is not a quality metric.

record.title: Ongoing research
record.body: NCT00672074 and NCT01280344 are completed interventional records. No active interventional program clearly testing ipamorelin was identified.

record.title: Main effects
record.body: This endogenous copper-binding tripeptide is studied for matrix remodeling, collagen-related signaling, wound repair, and skin biology. Positive work is largely preclinical or topical/cosmetic and does not establish systemic or injectable benefit.

record.title: Side effects
record.body: FDA says human safety information for injectable GHK-Cu is limited and flags immunogenicity, aggregation, and peptide-impurity concerns. Topical irritation is plausible; systemic copper and injectable risks remain poorly characterized.

record.title: Sourcing & pricing
record.body: Public 50 mg listings observed July 25–26, 2026 ranged from $58 to $64. Copper loading, identity, purity, and stability should be analytically confirmed for the intended experiment.

record.title: Ongoing research
record.body: Registry searches returned NCT07706361, a not-yet-recruiting patch study, and NCT07437586, a recruiting topical wound-healing record. Both are sponsor-submitted and neither supports injectable RUO use.
